record: P4S-31D — Platform voice capability feasibility matrix
mode: compile_only — feasibility verdicts, no implementation authorized by this artifact
doctrine: Every target captures locally and feeds the SAME Cockpit Chat intent rail (source='voice' -> /advisor/converse -> classify_intent -> intent loop -> proof). Wake-word / ambient verdicts are honest: no promise without defensible platform-documented feasibility. Device bindings reference infra/device_registry.json roles, never hostnames.

verdict_legend.PROVEN: path already exists and runs in this codebase (e.g. desktop-browser voice_server on :8096)
verdict_legend.LIKELY: standard, well-documented platform capability; low integration risk
verdict_legend.CONSTRAINED: possible but bounded by documented platform policy; requires a specific workaround and degrades outside it
verdict_legend.NOT_FEASIBLE: blocked by platform policy with no compliant path today
verdict_legend.UNKNOWN: cannot be asserted from platform documentation without a spike; must not be promised

shared_contract.proof_chain: substrate/execution/intent/loop.py submit -> AWAITING_APPROVAL -> governed approve -> PROOF_RECORDED (decided_by = Clerk principal)
shared_contract.tenant_identity_path: Clerk operator principal resolved server-side at /advisor/converse; identical to the principal that stamps decided_by (P4S-31C proven)
shared_contract.audio_policy: on-device capture; transcript-only transit by default; cloud-transcription DEFERRED to privacy review; no audio persistence by default
shared_contract.orchestrator_rule: the orchestrator-role node (per device_registry.json) NEVER has a microphone — no capture, no wake runtime on it

push_to_talk.why: already implemented and shipping: umh/voice_server.py on ws://:8096/voice, nginx /api/umh/voice/ws proxy, cockpit voiceStore mic state machine, RightRail mic affordance. STT = Groq Whisper with faster-whisper fallback; TTS = Kokoro (instance GPU node, per infra/device_registry.json) with espeak fallback.

wake_word.why: openWakeWord/Porcupine-class WASM can run in-tab, but a browser tab has no true background: wake detection only runs while the cockpit tab is foregrounded/active and the mic permission is granted for the origin. Backgrounded/discarded tabs suspend timers and may release the mic. No always-listening across app switches without a native shell.

ambient_always_on.why: requires the tab to stay foreground-active and mic-permitted; browsers throttle background tabs and may drop mic. Acceptable as 'ambient while cockpit tab is the active tab', NOT as system-wide always-on. Requires explicit VoiceConsentGrant(always_on).

targets.consent_surface: browser mic permission prompt (per-origin) + UMH VoiceConsentGrant(mode) stored state
risk_notes: autoplay policy: TTS playback needs a prior user gesture to unlock audio output
mic permission is per-origin and revocable in browser settings

targets.note: Electron cockpit shell (control_surface=electron_cockpit); VoiceCommandBar mounts only in Electron (Shell.tsx gate on window.cockpit).

push_to_talk.capture_api: Electron renderer getUserMedia (Chromium) OR native OS audio via main process; same :8096 voice_server path reused
push_to_talk.why: Electron has the same getUserMedia as desktop browser PLUS a persistent process, real background execution, and OS-level global shortcut registration for press-to-talk. Existing VoiceCommandBar already targets this shell.

wake_word.why: Electron main process can host an on-device wake runtime (openWakeWord/Porcupine native or platform-native) with a real background thread — no tab-throttling limit. This is the cleanest desktop wake path. Still gated by VoiceConsentGrant(wake_word).

ambient_always_on.why: technically feasible (persistent process, background thread, on-device detection) but held to CONSTRAINED by DOCTRINE, not platform limits: always_on ships LAST and only under an explicit, revocable VoiceConsentGrant(always_on) with an on-device wake runtime and CPU/battery budget. No decision to run cloud STT ambiently (deferred to privacy review).

targets.consent_surface: OS mic permission (macOS TCC / Windows privacy) + UMH VoiceConsentGrant(mode)
targets.tenant_identity_path: Clerk session in the Electron renderer -> /advisor/converse
risk_notes: global shortcut for push-to-talk must not conflict with OS bindings

targets.note: native iOS/Android app; controller role per device_registry.json (mobile device_type).

push_to_talk.capture_api: iOS AVAudioEngine/AVAudioRecorder + AVAudioSession; Android AudioRecord/MediaRecorder; stream PCM to :8096 voice_server or transcribe on-device
push_to_talk.why: foreground push-to-talk with an explicit mic button is a standard, documented capability on both platforms. Requires NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (iOS) / RECORD_AUDIO permission (Android).

wake_word.why: iOS: continuous background mic requires the 'audio' UIBackgroundMode + an active AVAudioSession, which Apple restricts to genuine audio apps; App Review commonly rejects always-listening mic used for non-audio features. Porcupine/openWakeWord can run on-device in the FOREGROUND cleanly. Android: a foreground service with microphoneType + a persistent notification is the documented compliant path (Android 10+ restricts background mic; Android 14 tightens FGS types). So: foreground wake LIKELY; background wake CONSTRAINED (Android via FGS) to NOT_FEASIBLE (iOS non-audio-app).

sub_verdicts.ios_background: NOT_FEASIBLE — iOS does not permit continuous background microphone for a non-audio utility app; background audio mode + App Review policy block it. No compliant always-on-mic path today.
sub_verdicts.ios_foreground: CONSTRAINED — foreground ambient only, screen-on, under explicit consent.
sub_verdicts.android_background: CONSTRAINED — possible via a foreground service (FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE, persistent notification, Android 14 FGS type declaration), user-visible and battery-costly; on-device wake runtime required.
sub_verdicts.android_foreground: CONSTRAINED — foreground ambient feasible under consent.

ambient_always_on.why: NO ambient/always-on mobile promise. iOS background is NOT_FEASIBLE for our use case; Android background is CONSTRAINED behind a foreground service. Any ambient mobile work is deferred and gated on a defensible platform spike + privacy review + VoiceConsentGrant(always_on).

targets.consent_surface: OS mic permission (iOS TCC / Android runtime permission) + UMH VoiceConsentGrant(mode)
risk_notes: iOS App Review rejects always-listening mic for non-audio apps
Android 14 requires declared FGS type for microphone foreground services
battery drain makes always-on hostile UX on mobile

targets.note: cockpit as a PWA / mobile web (client_type=mobile_browser).

push_to_talk.capture_api: web getUserMedia; iOS Safari requires a direct user gesture to start capture and to unlock audio output
push_to_talk.why: foreground press-to-talk works on modern mobile browsers, but iOS Safari is strict: getUserMedia and audio playback both require an explicit user gesture, and capture stops when the tab backgrounds or the screen locks. Usable for tap-to-talk; not for hands-free.

wake_word.why: mobile browsers have no background execution and aggressively suspend backgrounded tabs and release the mic; iOS Safari has no service-worker background audio and no wake-word API. A PWA cannot listen for a wake word while backgrounded or screen-locked. No compliant path.

ambient_always_on.why: same as wake-word: no background mic, tab suspension, screen-lock releases capture. Ambient on mobile browser is not achievable. Explicitly NOT promised.

targets.consent_surface: browser mic permission (per-origin, ephemeral on iOS) + UMH VoiceConsentGrant(push_to_talk only)
risk_notes: iOS Safari drops mic on tab background / screen lock
PWA has no reliable background execution for audio

wake_word.preferred_host: desktop_app (Electron main process, on-device runtime, real background thread)
wake_word.why: the ONLY clean ambient-wake path is the Electron desktop app running an on-device wake runtime in the main process. Desktop browser can approximate it while the cockpit tab is foreground-active. Both gated by VoiceConsentGrant(wake_word/always_on) and an on-device runtime with a CPU budget.

ambient_always_on.why: ships LAST, on desktop_app, on-device only, under explicit revocable consent, with a CPU/battery budget. No cloud STT ambiently without privacy review.

targets.consent_surface: OS mic permission + UMH VoiceConsentGrant(wake_word) then (always_on)
risk_notes: on-device wake runtime CPU budget must respect the CPU Gate Law
no wake runtime EVER on the orchestrator-role node (no mic on the VPS)

sub_verdicts.mobile_app_foreground: LIKELY — on-device Porcupine/openWakeWord in the foreground under consent
sub_verdicts.mobile_app_background_android: CONSTRAINED — foreground service (FGS microphone type, persistent notification) required; battery-costly
sub_verdicts.mobile_app_background_ios: NOT_FEASIBLE — non-audio app cannot hold continuous background mic; App Review policy blocks it
sub_verdicts.mobile_browser: NOT_FEASIBLE — no background execution / tab suspended / mic released

wake_word.why: NO mobile ambient wake-word promise. The only feasible slice is foreground on-device wake in the native mobile app. Background wake is CONSTRAINED (Android, via FGS) or NOT_FEASIBLE (iOS non-audio app; mobile browser). Any work here is deferred and gated on a platform spike + privacy review + VoiceConsentGrant(always_on).

ambient_always_on.why: true hands-free always-on across app switches / screen-lock is not compliantly achievable on iOS for a non-audio app, and is only a battery-hostile foreground-service approximation on Android. NOT promised. This row exists to record the honest constraint, not a roadmap commitment.

targets.consent_surface: OS mic permission + UMH VoiceConsentGrant(always_on) — required but insufficient given platform limits
risk_notes: iOS App Review is the binding blocker, not just an API limit
Android FGS mic is user-visible and drains battery
this row is CONSTRAINED/NOT_FEASIBLE by design — do not implement without owner sign-off after a spike
